page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 32 physical cores, utilizing the Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include any bundled local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core metrics. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance score of 1312.99 and single-threaded gzip compression speed of 22.8 GB/sec fall into the bottom 25% tier. Conversely, multi-threaded operations demonstrate solid mid-range performance, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 27991.83 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10040.0. Memory bandwidth is stable, recording 104.33 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 36.55 GB/sec for large block write operations. Database operations and web serving are also average, with Redis SET operations reaching 26.78 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 19.2 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation provides predictable compute resources for multi-threaded workloads, though the lack of local storage requires additional budget allocation for network storage. The primary tradeoff is the lower single-core performance, which makes it less optimal for single-threaded tasks. However, the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and strong multi-core scaling make this instance appropriate for parallel processing workloads, software compilation, static web serving, and distributed database operations.
